messages:
maria: Following up on the RFC — I sketched an "uncertainty contract" concept for low-bit paths (FP8/INT8/4-bit). Idea: runtime emits a small uncertainty token with each response so consumers can decide whether to accept, re-query, or fall back. Thoughts?

devon: love the idea. can you show what the token looks like? tiny JSON?

maria: sure, rough sketch: `{u: 0.12, mode: "calibrated", hint: "retry_if_gt_0.2"}` where u is normalized 0..1. runtime maintains calibration mapping per-model-version.

liam: question: where does calibration happen? during offline eval or online continuous calibrations?

maria: both. offline during profile onboarding we fit per-slice calibration curves. runtime emits raw signal + mapping id so the control plane can recompute drifted calibration.

sarah: what about cost surface? returning an extra token per-response tiny, but fallbacks cost more. we need a clear policy for clients so they don't overuse expensive fallbacks.

kai: propose a contract-level SLA: clients can pick one of (accept-any, conservative, quality-sla). conservative triggers fallback when u>t, quality-sla triggers rerun on a higher-precision variant and counts as a compensated hit against quota.

priyanka: ops question: how do we record these events for billing/observability? need to tag traces with `uncertainty.{raw,calibrated,decision}` so Console can roll up fallback rates and cost delta.

devon: runtime API surface: extend response envelope: `{ output: ..., meta: {uncertainty: {raw:0.13,calibrated:0.18,calib_id:"v1-2026-03"}, precision: "int8" } }` — clients ignore if they want.

liam: compatibility note: older SDKs should still get `output` only. default behavior server-side should be backwards compatible (no mandatory client changes).

maria: Agreed. default contract = accept-any to preserve existing semantics. advanced contracts opt-in via request headers or route config.

kai: security/attestation: to avoid clients gaming the signal, we should sign the `calib_id` and maybe a short HMAC of the raw signal; or mark as trust_level. Need to design for untrusted clients only reading the signal.

priyanka: telemetry: we'll want counters: `uncertainty_bucket[X]`, `fallback_rate_by_bucket`, `latency_delta_on_fallback`, `cost_delta_on_fallback`. Also link to prompt-set-triggered failures for regression alerts.

devon: experiment plan: A/B route where 10% of traffic has conservative contract with threshold 0.2 and compare quality (human eval or automated BLEU-like) and cost. measure false positive fallback rate (i.e., fallback but output was actually fine).

liam: definitions: false positive = fallback because u>t but higher-precision output was not measurably better. false negative = u<=t but low-bit output degraded quality. Need to estimate both per-customer.

sarah: per-customer calibration is huge. many customers have domain-specific distributions. must support per-customer calibrations or at least per-endpoint.

maria: plan: default global calibrations + per-tenant fine-tuning that customers can opt into during onboarding. per-tenant calibrations stored as small delta LUTs (calib_id per-tenant).

kai: rollout playbook: 1) offline calibration and sanity tests; 2) shadow `uncertainty` emission for 2 weeks on canary; 3) enable conservative contract in canary for 5% traffic; 4) increase and run human evals; 5) flip default if safe.

priyanka: add alerting: fallback_rate > 1% for a customer -> pager. quality-delta > threshold -> ticket to model ops.

devon: API ergonomics: suggest header `X-Redwood-Uncertainty: conservative;threshold=0.2;fallback=rerun:v2` or a JSON `serving_policy` field. keep header for lightweight clients.

liam: how do we handle streaming responses? uncertainty is token-level sometimes. do we emit a running mean or final aggregate?

maria: streaming: emit incremental `uncertainty` in stream chunks, plus final aggregate. for token-level decisions clients can do partial fallbacks but that's expensive. default use final aggregate.

kai: edge-case: hallucination detection systems may want different signals (semantic-certainty vs token-likelihood). we should expose multiple uncertainty dims e.g., {u_lm, u_sem, u_calib}. keep envelope extensible.

priyanka: storage: `calib_id` + compressed histogram snapshots. retention 90 days by default, longer for enterprise. exportable for customer audits.

maria: docs action items: write RFC addendum with: API shape, telemetry keys, rollout steps, experiment metric definitions, per-tenant calibration storage, HMAC attestation spec.

devon: ops-bot: noted. created ticket INF-4272 for RFC addendum and INF-4273 for console dashboard prototype. :white_check_mark:

maria: ok team — I'll draft the addendum and a small PoC service emitting `uncertainty` for int8/4bit paths. assign reviewers @devon @kai. thanks! :rocket:

liam: will start drafting the eval harness to compute false positives/negatives per-customer.

sarah: I'll pair with product on the customer contract language for fallback billing and SLA.

priyanka: I'll wire required telemetry and log keys into the schema.

ops-bot: INF-4272 assigned to maria, INF-4273 assigned to priyanka.
